name: Trigger.dev
summary: Trigger.dev is a background job platform where you write long-running tasks as normal async code, with built-in retries and scheduling.

free_plan_covers.note: Free plan gives $5 of usage credit a month rather than a fixed run count; a short task costs a fraction of a cent, so it stretches to roughly thousands of runs.

first_paid_usd_month.note: Hobby plan starts at $10/month for $10 of included usage credit and 50 concurrent runs.

portability.note: The platform is open source (Apache 2.0) and self-hostable, but tasks are written with Trigger.dev's own task() and schedules.task() SDK.

sdk_typescript.note: The @trigger.dev/sdk package is TypeScript-native and is the primary, documented way to define tasks.

long_running.note: Tasks execute indefinitely by default, with no forced cutoff, unless you opt into a maxDuration setting.

schedules.note: Cron-based scheduled tasks are built in via schedules.task(), though the free plan can't fire more than once an hour.

setup.step: Sign up at Trigger.dev and create a new project.
Run npx trigger.dev@latest init in your project to connect it and generate a trigger folder.
Install the SDK (@trigger.dev/sdk) and write your first task with task() or schedules.task().
Create an API key in the dashboard and set it as TRIGGER_SECRET_KEY in your environment file.
Run npx trigger.dev@latest dev locally, then deploy with npx trigger.dev@latest deploy.

builder_notes: Define scheduled jobs with schedules.task() and one-off background jobs with task(); trigger them from your app with tasks.trigger().
Keep TRIGGER_SECRET_KEY server-side only; it should never reach client-side code.
Free-plan cron schedules can't fire more than once per hour, so design around that if you need finer-grained timing.
